questions.text: Four processes arrive as follows. P1: arrival 0, burst 8. P2: arrival 1, burst 4. P3: arrival 2, burst 9. P4: arrival 3, burst 5. Under preemptive shortest-remaining-time-first scheduling, what is the average waiting time (in ms)?
questions.explain: Schedule: P1 runs 0-1, preempted by P2 (4 < 7). P2 runs 1-5. At t=5 remaining are P1=7, P3=9, P4=5, so P4 runs 5-10, then P1 10-17, then P3 17-26. Waiting = turnaround - burst: P1=9, P2=0, P3=15, P4=2. Average = 26/4 = 6.5.

questions.text: A counting semaphore S is initialised to 10. Six P (wait) operations and four V (signal) operations are then executed on S, and none of the waiting processes is blocked indefinitely. What is the final value of S?
questions.explain: Each P decrements, each V increments: 10 - 6 + 4 = 8.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT guaranteed by a correct solution to the critical section problem?
options: Equal CPU time for every competing process
questions.explain: The three requirements are mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting. Fair CPU distribution is a scheduling concern, not a critical-section requirement.

questions.text: A system has 5 processes, each of which may need a maximum of 3 units of a single resource type R. What is the minimum number of units of R that guarantees the system can never deadlock?
questions.explain: Worst case: every process holds max-1 = 2 units and waits. That is 5 x 2 = 10 units allocated with everyone blocked. One extra unit lets some process finish, so 11 units suffice.

questions.text: A cycle in the resource allocation graph is a necessary and sufficient condition for deadlock when:
options: Every resource type has exactly one instance
Every resource type has multiple instances
Processes request resources in increasing order of index
questions.explain: With single-instance resources a cycle means deadlock. With multiple instances a cycle is necessary but not sufficient - the claim edges may still resolve.

questions.text: Consider the page reference string 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with three frames, all initially empty. How many page faults occur under FIFO replacement?
questions.explain: FIFO produces 9 faults. Note LRU on the same string gives 10 - this string is the standard demonstration that more frames or a 'smarter' policy does not always help.

questions.text: A machine uses 32-bit virtual addresses with 4 KB pages and a single-level page table whose entries are 4 bytes each. What is the size of the page table in megabytes?
questions.explain: 4 KB pages means a 12-bit offset, leaving 20 bits of page number, so 2^20 entries. 2^20 x 4 bytes = 4 MB.

questions.text: TLB access takes 10 ns and main memory access takes 100 ns. The TLB hit ratio is 90 percent. On a TLB miss the page table is read from main memory before the data is fetched. What is the effective memory access time in nanoseconds?
questions.explain: Hit path: 10 + 100 = 110 ns. Miss path: 10 + 100 (page table) + 100 (data) = 210 ns. EMAT = 0.9 x 110 + 0.1 x 210 = 99 + 21 = 120 ns.

questions.text: A C program executes fork(); fork(); fork(); with no error checking and no exits. Counting the original process, how many processes exist in total after all three calls complete?
questions.explain: Each fork doubles the process count: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8. Seven of the eight are children.

questions.text: The disk head is at cylinder 53. Pending requests are 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67. Under SSTF, what is the total head movement in cylinders?

An inode holds 10 direct block pointers, one single indirect, one double indirect and one triple indirect pointer. Block size is 1 KB and each pointer is 4 bytes. What is the largest file size representable, approximately?
questions.explain: A block holds 1024/4 = 256 pointers. Direct 10 blocks, single indirect 256, double 256^2 = 65536, triple 256^3 = 16777216 blocks. Triple indirect dominates: 16777216 KB is about 16 GB.

questions.text: Which of the following are valid inter-process communication mechanisms in a Unix-like system? Select all that apply.
options: The process control block of another process
questions.explain: Pipes, shared memory and message queues are standard IPC. A PCB lives in kernel space and is not directly accessible to another process.
